title: ci: compile objectui against @objectstack/spec@main as the shape gate (objectui#9860)
body:
Part of #9860 — and #9860 remains open on purpose: see **What is left, and whose it is** below. This pull request lands the job; the half that makes it REQUIRED is a repository setting no file in this tree can write.

Clause-②: no — this adds a CI job; it moves no exported symbol, no key on a published payload, and relaxes no accept set.

Executes the maintainer's ruling of 2026-09-18, **option C**, recorded verbatim on the card: a real consumer compiling against objectstack `main` is the only shape gate for `@objectstack/spec`'s public surface. objectui is the first consumer. The direction is not re-adjudicated here.

> ⚠️ **Section added by the `domain:ui#2` execution seat** (PM session `session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`), 2026-09-20, after a refresh-and-re-measure round on this branch. ⛔ Nothing below was rewritten; two things it describes have changed, and both are repairs to this PR's own surface inside its existing 6 files.
>
> **① The compile step is now `--continue`.** Where this body says the job runs `TURBO_FORCE=true pnpm type-check`, it now appends `--continue`. Reason, measured: turbo stops scheduling at the first failing task, so the diagnostic set this gate reported was **a lower bound, always**. And because the one long-lived break is the objectui#9874 fixture, **every run stopped there** — no other package's drift against the spec had ever been measured. On real CI, two runs apart: **30 tasks → 81 tasks**, 51 of them never asked before. The verdict is unchanged (turbo still exits non-zero); only its completeness is.
>
> **② Attribution now fires on a GitHub Actions runner.** turbo carries the package name in a `package:task` prefix under STREAM log order (what you see locally) and in a group header under GROUPED order (what it selects on a runner) — and only grouped order ever reaches this job. The prefix-only parser therefore matched nothing, fell through to a package-relative path, and left the unmapped-package list EMPTY, so the summary did not even warn. ⇒ the one file the gate named was **openable by nobody**. Confirmed on CI: the shape-break annotation's path read `src/hooks/...` on both earlier runs and reads `packages/react/src/hooks/...` now.
>
> **Today's diagnostic set, on the refreshed head:** exactly **one**, and it is the one objectui#9874 owns. 80 of 81 tasks succeed. ⛔ The fixture was not touched.

## What lands

`.github/workflows/spec-main-shape-gate.yml` — check name **Spec Main Shape Gate**. On every pull request (no path filter) and on merge-queue builds it resolves objectstack `main` to a sha, fetches `packages/spec` at that sha, builds it, injects the result into this repository's install, and runs `TURBO_FORCE=true pnpm type-check`.

`scripts/spec-main-shape-gate.mjs` — the two halves the job calls: `inject` (replace and prove) and `report` (attribute and refuse).

## The acceptance criterion, demonstrated on a real break

The card's criterion is that a red names **which objectui file fails against which objectstack commit**. That is not a plan here; the gate was run end to end against `objectstack-ai/objectstack@96cf32b07579c0cafb6d9e58bb51930cef48e48d` (2026-09-18T11:42:52Z) and it is **RED**, on exactly one file:

```
packages/core/src/utils/normalize-list-view.ts(205,3): error TS2353: Object literal may only
specify known properties, and 'page' does not exist in type 'Record<"list" | "detail", string | null>'.
```

The report step turns that into a GitHub annotation on line 205 of `packages/core/src/utils/normalize-list-view.ts` carrying the objectstack short sha, plus a run-summary table pairing the file with a link to that commit. The file's own comment says the record is total over the spec's list "so a member the spec adds must be classed as drawable or explained HERE" — the removal direction breaks it the same way, which is the drift option C exists to see.

**Controlled, not assumed.** The same injection mechanism, same command, published bytes instead of main's:

| leg | injected | `turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/core` | diagnostics |
|---|---|---|---|
| control | published `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` from npm | exit 0 | 0 |
| subject | built from `objectstack@96cf32b07579` | exit 2 | 1 (the TS2353 above) |

So the break is objectstack `main` versus the published pin, not the mechanism.

**A second, independent drift** the compiler does not see: with main's spec installed, `scripts/__tests__/vite-objectstack-spec-dist.test.ts` fails 2 of 41 — the set of exports entries carrying a `browser` arm moves from `./cloud` to `./api`. Same two legs, same file: 41/41 pass on the published spec, 39/41 on main's. That is an existing pin doing its job at the next pin bump, reported here and **not** fixed here.

## The three questions the dispatch asked, each with its number

**1. The fetch shape — sparse checkout, decided by bytes received.** Three shapes, all measured on 2026-09-18 in one container against this same commit, with curl's and git's own counters (`--write-out` for the tarball, `du -sb` on `.git` for the clones):

| shape | transferred | wall | working tree |
|---|---|---|---|
| depth-1 **full clone** (the shape the discussion excluded) | 62,558,496 B `.git` (59.7 MiB) | 11.56 s | 199,927,528 B |
| codeload **packed tarball** at the sha | 57,379,106 B (54.7 MiB) | 8.77 s | n/a |
| **blobless + depth-1 + cone-sparse** (`packages/spec`, `scripts`) | 19,940,256 B `.git` (19.0 MiB) | 7.43 s (1.09 s clone + 6.34 s materialise) | 67,493,110 B |

**19.0 MiB against 54.7 MiB is the number that decided it** — 2.88x less than the tarball and 3.14x less than the full clone. The tarball loses for a structural reason, not a marginal one: codeload has no server-side path filter, so it ships the whole repository however little the job needs. ⚠️ Taken through this container's egress proxy, so the SECONDS are indicative and the BYTES are the claim.

The cone holds `scripts` as well as `packages/spec` because the spec's own build script calls scripts from the objectstack repository root; a cone holding only `packages/spec` fails in its build step.

**2. The mechanism — pnpm's virtual store, after a frozen-lockfile install.** This was the non-obvious one. objectui consumes a published `@objectstack/spec` through a caret range in many manifests plus a `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolution, and the pin-bump question is fenced off as still open.

- `OBJECTSTACK_SPEC_DIST` (`scripts/vite-objectstack-spec-dist.ts`) already resolves the spec at a locally built one — but it emits **Vite `resolve.alias`** entries, and `tsc` does not read a Vite config. A typecheck under it compiles against the *installed* spec: a green that means nothing. It stays the right hook for the console build.
- `pnpm.overrides` / `file:` / `link:` all move `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, a `package.json` or the lockfile. Every one of those is the pin.
- What the job does instead: after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, replace the contents of `node_modules/.pnpm/@objectstack+spec@*/node_modules/@objectstack/spec` with the built package. Nothing tracked by git is touched; a normal build resolves exactly what it resolved before.

Two things make that safe rather than clever, both measured:

- **Remove-then-copy, never copy-over.** The installed files are hardlinks into pnpm's global content-addressable store: `stat -c %h` on the installed spec's `package.json` read **7** before injection and **1** after. Writing *through* a hardlink would corrupt `@objectstack/spec` for every checkout on the machine and for whatever `actions/setup-node`'s pnpm cache saves afterwards.
- **The verification asks the consumers, not the injector.** "I replaced 1 directory" is a statement about the injector; the run prints `29 workspace consumer(s) verified on it` because it resolves every workspace symlink and refuses if any lands on a copy it did not inject.

The injected bytes come from `npm pack` (2,039 files, 28,685,157 B for this commit), so what objectui compiles against is the file set a release from that commit would ship — and a spec built with declarations skipped is refused by name instead of failing every consumer with TS2307.

**A third trap, found while measuring: the turbo cache is a false green here.** turbo's hash covers this repository's sources, its lockfile and a declared env list — never the *content* of `node_modules`, which is the only thing this job changes. A cached `type-check` therefore replays a verdict taken against a different spec, including the published one, and a run at a new objectstack sha replays the old sha's answer. The job runs with `TURBO_FORCE=true` and no cache action; the pin test holds it there. Observed on the real run: `force_executed_tasks=17`, `cache_hits=0`.

**3. "REQUIRED" is NOT mine to set — and this repository already knows it.** Requiredness is GitHub ruleset **11776024**, repository settings. `scripts/check-required-check-set.mjs` exists precisely because that surface can be READ from a job with network and written by nothing in this tree; its header states the read half and the write half separately. So this pull request does not claim the check is required. It makes it **requirable**, which is the part that is in the tree:

- unfiltered `pull_request` — a check that does not report on every pull request cannot be required (#3523: it leaves the PR pending until the ruleset's 60-minute timeout);
- subscribes `merge_group` — so a maintainer can enrol it *alone*, without the enrolment stalling every queued pull request. That ordering is #3523's, paid for once already;
- no `continue-on-error`; a shape break is a real red.

## What is left, and whose it is

`Maintainer-action:` **enrol the context `Spec Main Shape Gate` in ruleset 11776024**, and move its name from `NOT_A_GATE` to `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` in `scripts/dependabot-merge-gate.mjs` (one line; the merge-queue floor is already satisfied).

⚠️ **Not before the day-one break clears.** Enrolling it while the gate is red would turn every objectui pull request red over an objectstack commit — the shape objectui#6596 names, where a permanently red check teaches everyone to ignore red. Both conditions are written into the `NOT_A_GATE` entry so the next reader does not have to reconstruct them. Until then the check reports, annotates and goes red honestly; it just does not stop a merge.

⛔ Deliberately not decided here, because the card fences them off: who bumps the pin, cloud's half of option C, and whether `packages/core` or objectstack answers the `page` break.

## Tests and gates

Run on this branch; the commands and their real verdicts:

| command | verdict |
|---|---|
| `node scripts/spec-main-shape-gate.mjs --self-test` | exit 0 — 13/13 |
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/` | 5171 passed, 2 skipped, **1 file failed** — `vite-objectstack-spec-dist.test.ts`, caused by the injected spec still being in this checkout's `node_modules`, proven by the two legs above (41/41 with the published spec restored) |
| `pnpm type-check:scripts` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm type-check` (baseline, published spec, cold turbo cache) | exit 0 — 81 tasks, 6m18s |
| `TURBO_FORCE=true pnpm type-check` (main's spec injected) | exit 2 — the TS2353 above; this is the gate working |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | exit 0 — 7936 tracked text files |
| `node scripts/check-action-ref-convention.mjs` | exit 0 — 123 refs, 0 off-convention |
| `node scripts/check-pre-install-import-graph.mjs` | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-shell-escape-residue.mjs` | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 0 — no published source or contract moved, so no changeset is owed |
| `node scripts/check-new-cross-file-line-citations.mjs` | exit 0 — 0 new citations |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on the final file list | NOT GOVERNED — 0 of 5 paths matched |

The heavy runs went through the shared verify lock and their seconds are shared-box seconds, not idle-box ones.
